requirements.requirement: Enforce minimum password length of 12 characters for new user passwords on node1
requirements.summary: pwquality.conf set minlen=12 via cmd-7784b8bb1da04b97, confirmed by grep both pre- and post-restart (cmd-07df2869baf642a9, cmd-f6589b43a1864bb3). Directly demonstrated by rejecting a <12-char password for a real non-root user both before restart (cmd-e65599096be4447d, 'shorter than 12 characters') and after restart with a fresh user (cmd-87f139c3e87b42d7).

requirements.requirement: Enforce minimum of 3 different character classes for new user passwords on node1
requirements.summary: pwquality.conf set minclass=3 (cmd-7784b8bb1da04b97), confirmed pre/post restart. Directly demonstrated: a 13-char all-lowercase password was rejected with 'less than 3 character classes' both before (cmd-c84b65398e2d411e) and after restart (cmd-87f139c3e87b42d7), and a compliant 4-class password was accepted (cmd-5bf54f2c54e843ea, cmd-87f139c3e87b42d7).

requirements.requirement: Policy applies to new (non-root) user password changes, not just root-forced resets
requirements.summary: All enforcement tests were run as the actual pwtestuser/pwtestuser2 via 'su -s /bin/sh -c passwd', invoking pam_pwquality in the standard user-initiated passwd flow, not an administrative bypass.

requirements.requirement: Policy persists after a node restart (durability of configuration change)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id f9bf293d... captured (cmd-07df2869baf642a9), restart issued (cmd-0caf4ad30abe47ee), node briefly unreachable (cmd-c3e76e885cea4889) then recovered with new boot_id d26f66da... (cmd-c3921663cffe4acb), matching the fixed lifecycle snapshot boot-identity change. Config and enforcement were re-verified live post-restart with a fresh test user.

overall_summary: The executor correctly configured pam_pwquality with minlen=12 and minclass=3 in /etc/security/pwquality.conf on node1, verified pam-auth-update wired pam_pwquality.so into /etc/pam.d/common-password, and directly demonstrated end-to-end enforcement (reject <12 chars, reject <3 classes, accept compliant password) using real self-service password changes by non-root test users, both before and after a full node restart with a confirmed boot_id change. Test user accounts were cleanly removed and no unexplained residue or damaged package/service state remains.
limitations: The provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol was effectively satisfied for node1 as part of task-specific testing (pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, differing boot_id, recovered config/enforcement state), so no gap exists there.
Evidence is limited to the single managed node1; no other nodes are in scope per the topology.

Command outputs show redacted password text ('[REDACTED]'), which is expected security masking and does not impede verification of pass/fail outcomes via the surrounding pwquality error messages and exit codes.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor-created state (pwtestuser, pwtestuser2 accounts and their home directories) was fully removed and confirmed via 'no such user' checks (cmd-81dfc3ff8a5a4fd5, cmd-2589c1e6daaf469b, cmd-fbedbf70d1d942dd). Package installation (libpam-pwquality and dependencies) is a required, expected, retained change directly tied to the task outcome. The initial weak password set as root for pwtestuser (cmd-4a35acc81e824b59) bypassed the policy, but this was a necessary prerequisite to establish an authenticated initial credential for subsequent self-service passwd testing, not a policy violation, and the user was deleted afterward. The reboot (cmd-0caf4ad30abe47ee) was a bounded, purposeful action to validate persistence, with a healthy pre/post transition observed. Failed-services and package-health snapshots show no residue after executor changes. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found.
